description: Walk from copper birds and bronze Beatles through a legendary cellar to Britain's most flamboyant Victorian pub.
short_description: Meet Liver Birds, four bronze lads, 292 gigs and one outrageous pub.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
recommended_age: Recommended 10+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A waterfront-to-Hope-Street walk on public pavements with busy road crossings and a sustained uphill finish.

before_you_go.terrain: A waterfront-to-Hope-Street walk on public pavements with busy road crossings and a sustained uphill finish.
before_you_go.hills: A sustained uphill section leads away from the waterfront.
before_you_go.steps: No required steps are known, though temporary diversions may vary.
before_you_go.accessibility: Public pavements and paths throughout; check current diversions if step-free access is essential.
before_you_go.toilets: Check local public facilities before setting off; customer toilets may depend on opening hours.
before_you_go.footwear: Supportive, grippy walking shoes are recommended.
before_you_go.dogs: Outdoor route; keep dogs under control and check the final venue’s current dog policy.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Generally possible on public paths; check temporary diversions and busy crossings.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Begin beneath two copper guardians: one watches the city, the other the sailors on the Mersey.
stops.Hint_1: Go to Pier Head and find the clock-towered member of the Three Graces.
stops.Hint_2: Look up at the pair of Liver Birds on the Royal Liver Building.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Completed in 1911, the Royal Liver Building was among the world's earliest large reinforced-concrete buildings. Two 18-foot copper Liver Birds designed by Carl Bernard Bartels crown its clock towers.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find four lads forever striding beside the river, instruments absent but tiny personal symbols hidden.
stops.Hint_1: Stay on Pier Head near the Mersey ferry terminal.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the life-size bronze figures of John, Paul, George and Ringo.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Sculptor Andy Edwards's Beatles statue was unveiled in December 2015, marking 50 years since the band's final Liverpool performance. The Cavern Club donated the work to the city.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Leave daylight for a famous cellar where jazz began and four local lads returned 292 times.
stops.Hint_1: Walk inland to Mathew Street in the Cavern Quarter.
stops.Hint_2: Find the club entrance beneath its familiar red-lettered sign.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The Cavern Club opened as a jazz venue on 16 January 1957. The Beatles played 292 gigs here between February 1961 and August 1963, helping turn the cellar into a landmark of popular music.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Finish where music is carved into stone and Victorian drinking reaches a marble-and-mahogany crescendo.
stops.Hint_1: Climb through the city towards Hope Street and Philharmonic Hall.
stops.Hint_2: Find the ornate pub at number 36, opposite the concert hall.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! Walter W. Thomas designed the Philharmonic Dining Rooms for brewer Robert Cain in 1898-1900. This Grade I-listed pub preserves exceptional Art Nouveau gates and lavish interiors, and serves food and drink if open.
